messages:
incident-bot: ALERT -> model-serving-eviction-rate HIGH on prod-cluster-eu. Auto-pages sent to #eng-oncall. Summary: sudden spike in KV cache evictions causing tail latency and degraded throughput on text-generation endpoints.

maya: taking night shift as primary. I saw the page; joining the bridge. ETA 2m.

jon: I'm secondary for the night, available for escalations. If we need infra-level changes ping me.

maya: quick state: alert firing ~5m ago. Affected pools: gen-v2-eu-1 and rerank-v1-eu. Error logs show repeated OOM-evict warnings. Some customers seeing 504s on long-context requests. No full cluster outage.

samir: adding datapoints — metric snapshot (last 10m):
```
evictions/sec: gen-v2-eu-1 = 48 -> 180
p90-latency-s2s: 220ms -> 980ms
active-requests: steady
free-gpu-memory: down 12% per node
```
Looks like memory pressure + increased tail queries.

maya: mitigations in progress: 1) temporarily increase eviction-threshold on gen pools (safe +10%); 2) spin a small 2-node burst pool gen-v2-eu-burst; 3) enable prefix-KV cache bypass for long-context customers.

jon: I deployed the threshold bump to gen-v2-eu-1 via the ops pipeline. Command used:
```
opsctl set-flag --cluster=prod-cluster-eu --pool=gen-v2-eu-1 --eviction-threshold=0.67
```
No rollback yet. Monitoring.

maya: samir, can you start the burst nodes? Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/model-eviction (section: "burst-capacity-and-thresholds").

samir: starting burst now. Spawn jobs 2/2 queued. ETA ~90s.

ops-bot: spawn-job status -> job-83912 queued; logs: provisioning GPUs.

maya: customer impact note for handoff: potential degraded responses for customers on gen-v2 with >8k tokens. We've flagged customer-ACME and customer-SOURCE for support to preempt escalations. No public incident page yet.

jon: we're also seeing increased retry rates at the API gateway for embeddings. Not sure if related, but watch emb-queue-length.

maya: good call — add emb-queue alert to watchlist. samir, after burst is up, can you begin graceful draining of most-evicting hosts? Use drain-runbook section.

samir: drain started on node prod-eu-12 (highest evictions). Draining connections, will move workloads to burst.

maya: logs show queue backlog decreasing on gen-v2-eu-1 after threshold bump and the first burst node is ready. evictions/sec dropping to ~60. p95 latency improving.

incident-bot: NOTE -> alert suppression: per policy, suppress duplicate eviction alerts for the next 10m while we stabilize.

jon: are there any known rolling deploys or customer spikes? I checked deploys — nothing in the last 30m. Traffic profile shows a sudden cohort of long-context requests from EU region. Could be a customer integration test.

maya: outreach: support, please DM customers we flagged. I can draft a blurb.

tara: (support) on it. I'll reach out to ACME -> asking them to pause large-batch requests until we confirm stability.

maya: ongoing mitigations checklist (for handoff):
- [x] bump eviction threshold on gen-v2-eu-1
- [x] provision 2-node burst (1 active, 1 on standby)
- [x] drain high-eviction nodes to burst
- [ ] monitor for 20m window after drains complete
- [ ] verify no 5xxs for top 10 customers

samir: note: one node (prod-eu-09) failed graceful drain due to stuck pods; I restarted kubelet on that host and it's rejoining. Will follow up.

maya: coverage: I'm primary until 07:00 UTC. Jon will continue as secondary until 10:00 UTC. After that, night rotation has a gap 10:00-11:00 UTC where oncall-secondary is unassigned (known schedule gap). Tara, can you cover escalation if we see a re-escalation during that hour?

tara: I can cover 10:00-11:00 UTC if needed. I'll tentative-claim in the schedule.

jon: I plan to stay on until 10:15 UTC to help transition. If anything spikes after 10:15, hand to tara.

maya: handoff notes to next primary (jon -> tara if needed):
- Active alerts: model-serving-eviction-rate (suppressed until +10m), emb-queue-length (watching), api-gateway-retry-rate (info)
- Mitigations: threshold bump deployed, 1/2 burst nodes online, draining in progress, support notified for top two customers
- Known risks: stuck-kubelet node prod-eu-09 (restarted), schedule gap 10:00-11:00 UTC
- Runbook pointers: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/model-eviction (steps 2-4), opsctl docs: https://internal.redwood.ai/opsctl#set-flag
- Escalation path: if p95 > 1s or >5% 5xx across top 20 customers -> page infra-leads + exec-oncall

samir: metric snapshot after burst + drains (T+7m): evictions/sec -> 22, p95 -> 370ms, 5xx rate -> 0.6% (was 2.1%). Good improvement.

maya: thanks team — I'll stay on-call for the next 25m and then hand to jon. If we get another page, we will re-open the bridge and escalate.

jon: copied. I'll watch dashboards and keep an eye on support threads. If we need config rollback, I have the commands and creds.

tara: noted. I'll be reachable via DM during the gap and can jump on if we need an extra pair of hands.

ops-bot: bridge created -> https://meet.redwood.ai/bridge/incident-2123456789 (recording enabled).

maya: closing the thread for now — putting a short summary into the incident tracker and will update if anything changes. Leaving this thread as the handoff record.

jon: acknowledged. Thanks maya.

samir: ack. leaving monitoring.

incident-bot: THREAD SUMMARY: mitigation applied (threshold bump + burst + drains). Metrics trending toward normal. Monitoring period in progress.

maya: last check before handoff (T+18m): evictions stable, p95 ~360ms, no fresh 5xx spikes. handoff complete.
